chapter_summary: Six days before Passover, Jesus returns to Bethany. Mary pours expensive perfume on Jesus' feet in love. The next day, crowds wave palm branches as Jesus enters Jerusalem on a donkey — the King has come! Some Greeks ask to see Jesus. He says His hour has come. Like a seed that dies to bear fruit, He must die to bring life to many. A voice from heaven confirms His mission. Jesus declares He is the light of the world — believe in Him before darkness comes.
main_lesson: Jesus is the King who came to die so we could live. When we believe in Him — the Light of the world — we are brought out of darkness and into His life forever.

memory_verse.kjv: I am come a light into the world, that whosoever believeth on me should not abide in darkness.
memory_verse.little_bible: Jesus said: 'I am the Light of the world. Everyone who trusts in Me will not stay in the dark.'

parent_guide: John 12 is a chapter of dramatic turning points. It opens with Mary's extravagant act of worship (vv1-8) — a model of love that prioritises Jesus above cost or criticism. The Triumphal Entry (vv12-19) fulfils Zechariah 9:9 and publicly announces Jesus as King — yet His kingdom is not what the crowd expects. The Greeks seeking Jesus (vv20-22) signals that the Gospel is for all nations, not Israel alone. Jesus' seed-dying-to-bear-fruit teaching (v24) is the core of cross theology explained for everyone: death leads to life. The voice from heaven (v28) and Jesus' declarations about light and darkness (vv35-36, 46) give children a vivid framework: trust Jesus now, while the light is here. The chapter ends with Jesus' final public teaching before the cross. The hard truth of vv37-43 — people who saw miracles still refused to believe, and leaders who believed stayed silent from fear of people — gives parents a chance to discuss courageous faith vs. people-pleasing.
application_for_children: Mary showed her love for Jesus with everything she had. The crowds welcomed Jesus as King. You can welcome Jesus as your King today too! When you trust Jesus, He brings you out of darkness — like turning on a light in a dark room. He came to give you life. Trust the Light!

verses.kjv: Then Jesus six days before the passover came to Bethany, where Lazarus was which had been dead, whom he raised from the dead.
verses.little_bible: Six days before Passover, Jesus came to Bethany. Lazarus lived there — the man Jesus had raised from the dead.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus went to Bethany. His friend Lazarus was there — alive again!
verses.meaning: Jesus returned to the very place where He had done a great miracle. Lazarus, once dead, was now living proof of Jesus' power. The cross was six days away.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for coming close to us.
verses.discussion_question: Why was Lazarus so special to the people in Bethany?
verses.family_discussion: Lazarus had been raised from the dead — he was living proof that Jesus has power over death. How does knowing that encourage your family today?
verses.do_it_today: Thank God for one person in your life He has brought through something hard.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus walking along a dusty path toward a small village at dusk, a stone-walled house ahead, olive trees on either side, warm lamplight glowing in the window, calm and purposeful mood. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: There they made him a supper; and Martha served: but Lazarus was one of them that sat at the table with him.
verses.little_bible: They made a special dinner for Jesus. Martha served the food. Lazarus sat at the table with Jesus.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They had dinner with Jesus. Lazarus sat right beside Him!
verses.meaning: A meal was prepared in Jesus' honour. Martha served — that was her gift. Lazarus simply sat with Jesus. Both ways of showing love matter.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me serve You with joy.
verses.discussion_question: What is one way you can serve Jesus today?
verses.family_discussion: Martha cooked and served; Lazarus simply sat with Jesus. What gifts has God given each person in your family to serve Him?
verses.do_it_today: Serve someone at home today without being asked — as a gift to Jesus.
verses.illustration_prompt: A warm evening dinner scene in a Middle Eastern home, Jesus reclining at a table with Lazarus and friends, Martha carrying a bowl of food, lamplight casting a golden glow, joyful and peaceful atmosphere. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Then took Mary a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair: and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment.
verses.little_bible: Mary poured very expensive perfume on Jesus' feet. She wiped His feet with her hair. The whole house filled with the sweet smell.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Mary poured costly perfume on Jesus' feet. She dried them with her hair.
verses.meaning: Mary gave the most precious thing she had to Jesus. It was an act of total love and worship — nothing held back. The whole house could smell it. True worship cannot be hidden.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I want to give You my best.
verses.discussion_question: What is the most precious thing you could give to Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Mary gave something very expensive and personal to Jesus. What does it look like for your family to give Jesus your very best — not the leftovers?
verses.do_it_today: Give something you value — your time, a kind act, a prayer — to Jesus today.
verses.illustration_prompt: Mary kneeling at Jesus' feet, pouring perfume from a small alabaster bottle, her long dark hair spread over His feet, a soft fragrant mist rising, warm candlelight, reverent and beautiful scene. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Then saith one of his disciples, Judas Iscariot, Simon's son, which should betray him,
verses.little_bible: One of Jesus' twelve disciples was Judas Iscariot. He would one day hand Jesus over to His enemies.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A disciple named Judas was there. He would later betray Jesus.
verses.meaning: Judas is introduced with a shadow over him. He sat at the same table and watched the same miracle, but his heart was turned away from Jesus.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, keep my heart loyal to You always.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it dangerous to be close to Jesus but not really love Him?
verses.family_discussion: Judas walked with Jesus every day but never truly gave his heart. How can your family make sure you love Jesus, not just know about Him?
verses.do_it_today: Ask Jesus today: 'Is my heart really Yours?' Listen quietly.
verses.illustration_prompt: A man with a guarded, darkened expression sitting at a dinner table among friends, the other faces warm and open, lamplight illuminating the contrast in expressions, slightly foreboding atmosphere. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred pence, and given to the poor?
verses.little_bible: Judas asked: 'Why wasn't this perfume sold? It was worth a lot of money. It should have been given to the poor!'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Judas said: 'That perfume cost so much! It should have been sold to help the poor.'
verses.meaning: Judas made his complaint sound generous. But loving-sounding words can hide selfish hearts. Not every objection to worship is truly about helping others.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, make my heart honest and true.
verses.discussion_question: Can someone say the right words but have the wrong heart?
verses.family_discussion: Judas pretended to care about the poor. How can we check if our reasons for doing things are truly good — or just excuses?
verses.do_it_today: Ask yourself before you speak today: 'Is this really true, or am I making excuses?'
verses.illustration_prompt: A man pointing accusingly at a woman kneeling on the floor, his face set with displeasure, the other disciples looking on with uncertainty, warm lamp-lit interior. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag, and bare what was put therein.
verses.little_bible: Judas did not really care about the poor. He was a thief. He kept the money bag and stole from it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Judas did not care about the poor. He was stealing money from the bag.
verses.meaning: God sees what is truly in our hearts. Judas wore a disguise of concern, but inside he was greedy and dishonest. Sin hides — but not from God.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me be honest inside and out.
verses.discussion_question: Why can't we hide what is truly in our hearts from God?
verses.family_discussion: Judas looked like a good disciple on the outside but was dishonest inside. How can your family grow in being the same on the inside as you appear on the outside?
verses.do_it_today: Confess something to God that only He knows — He already sees it, and He loves you anyway.
verses.illustration_prompt: A man clutching a money bag with a furtive expression, shadows behind him while warm light shines on the others, a subtle contrast between outward appearance and inner reality. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Then said Jesus, Let her alone: against the day of my burying hath she kept this.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'Leave her alone. She kept this perfume for the day of My burial.' Jesus was talking about His coming death.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'Leave Mary alone. She saved this for My burial.'
verses.meaning: Jesus defended Mary's act of love. He also knew He was going to die soon. Mary may not have fully understood — but her act pointed to the cross.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for defending those who love You.
verses.discussion_question: Why did Jesus say Mary's gift was for His burial?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus was already thinking about His death — and He saw Mary's love as preparation for it. How does knowing Jesus died for us make us want to love Him more?
verses.do_it_today: Thank Jesus today specifically for what He did on the cross for you.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus standing with a calm, protective expression, hand extended toward Mary, Judas looking rebuked in the background, Mary looking up with gratitude and tears. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: For the poor always ye have with you; but me ye have not always.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'You will always have the poor to help. But I will not always be with you in this way.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'The poor will always need help. But I won't be here with you much longer.'
verses.meaning: Jesus was not dismissing care for the poor. He was saying: this moment of worship is irreplaceable. There are seasons for everything — and this was a season to honour Him.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me never take You for granted.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important to honour Jesus right now, today?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus said His time was short. As a family, how can you make sure you are making time for Jesus — not just fitting Him in?
verses.do_it_today: Set aside 5 minutes today just to be with Jesus — no rush, no phone, no noise.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus speaking gently to the disciples around a table, His expression peaceful but carrying a gentle sense of urgency, soft evening lamplight, a quiet and holy atmosphere. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there: and they came not for Jesus' sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead.
verses.little_bible: A large crowd heard Jesus was in Bethany. They came to see Jesus — and also to see Lazarus, who had been raised from the dead.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Many people came to see Jesus and Lazarus, who had been raised from the dead.
verses.meaning: Lazarus was living proof of Jesus' power. The miracle drew crowds. God uses transformed lives to point people to Jesus.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, let my life point others to You.
verses.discussion_question: How does seeing what God has done in someone's life make you want to know Jesus more?
verses.family_discussion: Lazarus's resurrection brought people running to see Jesus. How has Jesus changed someone in your family in a way that could point others to Him?
verses.do_it_today: Tell one person this week about something Jesus has done in your family.
verses.illustration_prompt: A large crowd of people walking along a dusty road toward a village, some pointing ahead excitedly, expressions of curiosity and wonder, hills and olive trees in the background, warm afternoon light. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death;
verses.little_bible: The chief priests made a plan. They wanted to kill Lazarus too.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The chief priests planned to kill Lazarus as well.
verses.meaning: The miracle that gave life became a threat to those who hated Jesus. Instead of believing, the priests planned more evil. Hardened hearts refuse even the greatest evidence.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, soften every hard heart to know You.
verses.discussion_question: Why would someone want to kill a man who had been brought back to life?
verses.family_discussion: The priests saw the miracle and still chose hatred. What does this tell us about the danger of a heart that refuses to trust God?
verses.do_it_today: Pray for someone you know who seems far from God — ask Jesus to soften their heart.
verses.illustration_prompt: A group of men in religious robes huddled in a torch-lit room, leaning together in a tense secret meeting, expressions dark and calculating, shadows heavy on the walls. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.
verses.little_bible: Because of Lazarus, many people were leaving the religious leaders and putting their trust in Jesus.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Many people saw Lazarus and chose to believe in Jesus.
verses.meaning: A living witness cannot be silenced easily. Lazarus simply being alive was enough to turn hearts toward Jesus. Lives changed by Jesus are powerful testimony.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, use my life to draw others to You.
verses.discussion_question: How can just being changed by Jesus help others believe in Him?
verses.family_discussion: Lazarus did not preach a sermon — he just lived. How is your family's daily life a testimony to what Jesus does?
verses.do_it_today: Live today in a way that shows you belong to Jesus — in kindness, patience, and joy.
verses.illustration_prompt: Groups of people turning and walking away from a crowd of religious leaders, moving toward the light where Jesus stands in the distance, hopeful expressions on their faces. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: On the next day much people that were come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,
verses.little_bible: The next day, a great crowd had come to the Passover feast. When they heard Jesus was coming to Jerusalem, they got excited.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The next day, crowds heard Jesus was coming to Jerusalem!
verses.meaning: The Passover crowd was already large — now word spread that Jesus was coming. Excitement grew. The city was about to welcome its King.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I am ready and glad You are coming.
verses.discussion_question: How do you feel when someone very special is about to arrive?
verses.family_discussion: The crowd's excitement grew the moment they heard Jesus was coming. How excited is your family about Jesus being in your life every day?
verses.do_it_today: Greet this day excited that Jesus is with you — not just on Sunday but right now.
verses.illustration_prompt: A large excited crowd near Jerusalem's city gates, people turning to each other with wide eyes and smiles, pointing down the road, palm trees and stone walls, bright daytime sky. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Took branches of palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.
verses.little_bible: The people took palm branches and ran out to meet Jesus. They shouted: 'Hosanna! Blessed is the King of Israel who comes in the name of the Lord!'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: People waved palm branches and shouted: 'Hosanna! Blessed is Israel's King!'
verses.meaning: 'Hosanna' means 'Save us now!' The crowd recognised Jesus as their coming King. They were right — though they did not yet understand that His kingdom would come through the cross.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are my King. Hosanna!
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to call Jesus your King?
verses.family_discussion: The crowd shouted 'Save us now!' — Hosanna. What does your family need Jesus to save you from today? Pray it out loud together.
verses.do_it_today: Shout or sing a praise to Jesus today — out loud, not in your head!
verses.illustration_prompt: A joyful crowd lining a road into Jerusalem, people waving large green palm branches overhead, faces lifted in praise, children in front, Jesus visible approaching in the distance on a donkey, bright sunny day. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: And Jesus, when he had found a young ass, sat thereon; as it is written,
verses.little_bible: Jesus found a young donkey and sat on it. This was exactly what the Scriptures had said would happen.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus sat on a young donkey — just as Scripture said He would.
verses.meaning: Jesus chose a humble animal, not a warhorse. The King of kings entered in peace, fulfilling prophecy written hundreds of years before. Scripture is always true.
verses.memory_phrase: Jesus came humbly, just as promised.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, Your Word always comes true.
verses.discussion_question: Why do you think Jesus chose a donkey instead of a horse?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus could have arrived any way He liked — but He chose humility. How can your family follow Jesus' example of being humble?
verses.do_it_today: Choose to do something humble today — serve someone without wanting credit.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus sitting serenely on a small young donkey, entering a road lined with palm branches, disciples walking alongside, the city of Jerusalem visible ahead, warm and peaceful. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Fear not, daughter of Sion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass's colt.
verses.little_bible: The Scripture said: 'Do not be afraid! Your King is coming, riding on a donkey's colt.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Scripture said: 'Don't be afraid. Your King is coming on a donkey!'
verses.meaning: God's message through the prophet Zechariah was: your King brings peace, not war. He comes to comfort, not to frighten. With Jesus as King, we need not fear.
verses.memory_phrase: Your King is coming. No fear.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, because You are my King, I will not be afraid.
verses.discussion_question: Why can we stop being afraid when Jesus is our King?
verses.family_discussion: God told His people 'fear not' because their King was coming. What fears can your family bring to Jesus the King today?
verses.do_it_today: Name one fear and then say out loud: 'Jesus is my King — I will not be afraid.'
verses.illustration_prompt: A peaceful scene of Jesus riding a young donkey toward Jerusalem, a golden glow around the path, people watching with relieved and joyful expressions, no swords or soldiers in sight. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: These things understood not his disciples at the first: but when Jesus was glorified, then remembered they that these things were written of him, and that they had done these things unto him.
verses.little_bible: At first, the disciples did not understand what was happening. Later, after Jesus rose again, they remembered — and understood it all.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The disciples did not understand. Later, after Jesus rose, they remembered and understood.
verses.meaning: Sometimes we do not understand what God is doing until later. The resurrection gave the disciples clarity to see what Scripture had always promised. Faith does not require understanding everything right now.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me trust You even when I do not understand.
verses.discussion_question: Has something ever made sense to you later that was confusing at first?
verses.family_discussion: The disciples were confused then understood later. When has your family trusted God through something confusing — and later seen His hand in it?
verses.do_it_today: Think of something confusing in your life. Tell God: 'I trust You even when I don't understand yet.'
verses.illustration_prompt: A group of disciples looking puzzled and whispering to each other, then a separate scene of the same disciples with expressions of wonder and understanding, light dawning on their faces. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: The people therefore that was with him when he called Lazarus out of his grave, and raised him from the dead, bare record.
verses.little_bible: The people who had seen Jesus call Lazarus out of the grave kept telling everyone about it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Eyewitnesses kept telling everyone about Lazarus being raised.
verses.meaning: Those who witnessed the miracle became witnesses. They could not stop talking about what they had seen. When God does something in your life, you become a witness too.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, let me tell others what You have done.
verses.discussion_question: If you saw someone raised from the dead, could you keep quiet about it?
verses.family_discussion: The eyewitnesses kept telling the story. What story about what Jesus has done in your family are you telling to others?
verses.do_it_today: Tell one person today about something Jesus has done for your family.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two people animatedly telling a small group of listeners about a miraculous event, eyes wide with excitement, hands gesturing, the listeners leaning in with wonder. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: For this cause the people also met him, for that they heard that he had done this miracle.
verses.little_bible: That is why the crowd came to meet Jesus — they had heard about the miracle He had done.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The crowd came because they heard Jesus had done an amazing miracle.
verses.meaning: One miracle, widely shared, drew an entire crowd to Jesus. The Gospel spreads when believers tell what they have seen and heard.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, use Your wonders to draw people to You.
verses.discussion_question: What happens when people hear what Jesus can do?
verses.family_discussion: The crowd came because they heard the news. Who in your neighbourhood needs to hear what Jesus has done so they can come too?
verses.do_it_today: Pray for one person to hear about Jesus this week — and think about how God might use you to share it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A crowd of curious people flowing from all directions toward a central road, word spreading between them, some holding children's hands, others running, a warm midday scene with the city in the background. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him.
verses.little_bible: The Pharisees said to each other: 'Nothing is working! Look — the whole world is following Jesus!'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The Pharisees said: 'Everyone is following Jesus! We cannot stop Him!'
verses.meaning: The Pharisees saw that their plans to stop Jesus were failing. In their frustration, they spoke more truth than they knew: the whole world would indeed come to Jesus.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, Your kingdom cannot be stopped.
verses.discussion_question: Why couldn't the Pharisees stop people from following Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Even Jesus' enemies admitted the whole world was going after Him. How does knowing that Jesus cannot be stopped encourage your faith?
verses.do_it_today: Write down one way you will follow Jesus today — on purpose, not by accident.
verses.illustration_prompt: A cluster of religious leaders in robes looking frustrated and alarmed, watching from a distance as enormous crowds follow after Jesus, helpless expressions, their plans clearly failing. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: And there were certain Greeks among them that came up to worship at the feast:
verses.little_bible: Some Greek people had also come to Jerusalem to worship at the Passover feast.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Some Greek visitors came to Jerusalem to worship God.
verses.meaning: Greeks — non-Jews — had come to worship. They represent the wider world hungry for God. Jesus came not just for one nation but for all people everywhere.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for welcoming everyone.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it wonderful that Jesus came for people from every nation?
verses.family_discussion: People from far-off places came seeking God. Who in your world — from a different background or country — needs to know Jesus?
verses.do_it_today: Pray for one person from a different background to hear about Jesus this week.
verses.illustration_prompt: A small group of visitors in different clothing from the local crowd, looking curiously at the temple and the celebration around them, expressions of sincere seeking and wonder. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: The same came therefore to Philip, which was of Bethsaida of Galilee, and desired him, saying, Sir, we would see Jesus.
verses.little_bible: These Greeks came to Philip and said: 'Sir, we want to see Jesus.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The Greeks said to Philip: 'Sir, we want to see Jesus!'
verses.meaning: 'We would see Jesus' — one of the most important requests in the Gospels. People are still asking this today. Our job is to bring them to Jesus.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me show You to others.
verses.discussion_question: How can you help someone who wants to see Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: 'We would see Jesus' — this is the cry of many people around you. How is your family making Jesus visible to the people in your lives?
verses.do_it_today: Introduce someone to Jesus today — through your words, actions, or a direct conversation.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two men in Greek-style robes speaking respectfully to a disciple named Philip, hopeful expressions on their faces, asking with open hands, Jerusalem's temple visible in the background. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Philip cometh and telleth Andrew: and again Andrew and Philip tell Jesus.
verses.little_bible: Philip went to Andrew. Then Andrew and Philip together brought the message to Jesus.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Philip told Andrew. Then Andrew and Philip told Jesus.
verses.meaning: Philip did not do it alone — he went to Andrew. Together they brought the need to Jesus. Teamwork and community matter in bringing people to Christ.
verses.memory_phrase: Together we bring people to Jesus.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me work with others for You.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it better to work together when helping people find Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Philip and Andrew worked together. How can your family team up to help someone come to Jesus?
verses.do_it_today: Partner with a friend or family member in one act of kindness or witness today.
verses.illustration_prompt: Philip whispering to Andrew, both disciples then walking together toward Jesus who stands in the distance, purpose on their faces, warm afternoon sunlight. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: And Jesus answered them, saying, The hour is come, that the Son of man should be glorified.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'The hour has come. It is time for the Son of Man to be glorified.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'The time has come. I am about to be glorified.'
verses.meaning: Jesus knew the cross was near. He called it His 'hour' — not an accident but an appointment. His death and resurrection would be His greatest glory.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for Your perfect timing.
verses.discussion_question: Why did Jesus call His death His hour of glory?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus knew what was coming and was not afraid. How does Jesus' courage at the cross give your family courage to face hard things?
verses.do_it_today: Face one hard or scary thing today with the words: 'God's timing is perfect.'
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus looking upward with calm resolve, sunlight framing His face, the disciples watching intently, an atmosphere of holy weight and significance. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'A seed that stays a seed produces nothing. But when it is planted and dies, it grows into something that bears much fruit.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'A seed must die in the ground before it grows and makes fruit.'
verses.meaning: Jesus used a seed to explain His death. He had to die so that life could come to many people. Death is not the end — it is the beginning of something far greater.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for dying so I could live.
verses.discussion_question: How is Jesus dying like a seed planted in the ground?
verses.family_discussion: A seed looks like it disappears — but it is actually becoming something greater. How does understanding the cross as a seed help you explain Easter to a friend?
verses.do_it_today: Plant a seed or water a plant today — let it remind you that Jesus died to bring you life.
verses.illustration_prompt: A small wheat seed falling toward dark rich soil, a glowing sprout beginning to emerge beneath, golden stalks of wheat visible in the background representing the harvest to come. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: He that loveth his life shall lose it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'Whoever tries to keep their life for themselves will lose it. Whoever gives their life to Me will keep it forever.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'Give your life to Me, and you will have life forever.'
verses.meaning: Jesus calls His followers to stop clinging to their own comfort and control. Surrendering your life to Jesus — not holding it tightly for yourself — is the path to eternal life.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I give my whole life to You.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to give your life to Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus says holding tightly to your own life is the way to lose it. What is one area your family can surrender more fully to Jesus?
verses.do_it_today: Tell Jesus: 'I give You today — my plans, my worries, my whole day.'
verses.illustration_prompt: A child opening hands upward as if releasing something into the sky, an expression of peace replacing a worried look, warm sunrise light, a sense of freedom and relief. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: If any man serve me, let him follow me; and where I am, there shall also my servant be: if any man serve me, him will my Father honour.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'If anyone serves Me, follow Me. Where I am, My servant will be too. And My Father will honour those who serve Me.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'Serve Me. Follow Me. God the Father will honour you.'
verses.meaning: Following Jesus is not just a decision — it is a daily walk. And where Jesus goes, His servants go. The reward is not just in heaven — the Father Himself honours those who serve His Son.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I want to follow You every day.
verses.discussion_question: What is one way you can serve and follow Jesus today?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus promises that those who serve Him will be with Him — and the Father will honour them. How does this promise motivate your family to serve Jesus this week?
verses.do_it_today: Do one act of service today as if you are doing it directly for Jesus.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus walking ahead on a path, a group of followers stepping in His footsteps, golden light ahead, the disciples expressions determined and joyful. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Now is my soul troubled; and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour: but for this cause came I unto this hour.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'My soul is deeply troubled. Should I say, Father, save Me? But no — this is exactly why I came.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'I am deeply troubled. But this is why I came.'
verses.meaning: Jesus was fully human — He felt the weight of what was coming. Yet He did not run. He faced the cross because He chose it. His love was stronger than His fear.
verses.memory_phrase: Jesus chose to face the cross.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for not running away from the cross.
verses.discussion_question: How does it help you to know Jesus felt troubled but still obeyed?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus was honest about His struggle — and still chose to obey. When something is hard, how can your family follow Jesus' example of honest prayer and faithful obedience?
verses.do_it_today: Tell God honestly about something that troubles you. Then say: 'But I trust You, God.'
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus alone in a quiet garden, face showing deep emotion, one hand pressed to His heart, looking upward in prayer, soft light filtering through the trees, atmosphere of holy struggle and surrender. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Father, glorify thy name. Then came there a voice from heaven, saying, I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.
verses.little_bible: Jesus prayed: 'Father, bring glory to Your name!' Then a voice came from heaven: 'I have already glorified it — and I will glorify it again.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus prayed: 'Father, glorify Your name!' God answered from heaven: 'I have and I will!'
verses.meaning: Jesus' deepest desire was not to escape pain but to glorify God. And God answered from heaven! The Father confirmed His plan. The cross and resurrection would both glorify God's name.
verses.memory_phrase: God, let Your name be glorified!
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, may everything I do bring glory to God.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to bring glory to God's name?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus prayed for God's glory, not His own comfort — and God answered aloud from heaven! What would it look like for your family's biggest desire to be God's glory?
verses.do_it_today: Before you start an activity today, pray: 'God, may this bring glory to Your name.'
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus with arms raised toward a golden-lit sky, a warm radiant beam of light descending from the heavens, bystanders covering their eyes or falling back in awe, an atmosphere of divine power and glory. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: The people therefore, that stood by, and heard it, said that it thundered: others said, An angel spake to him.
verses.little_bible: The crowd heard the voice from heaven. Some thought it was thunder. Others thought an angel had spoken.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The crowd heard the voice. Some said thunder. Others said an angel spoke.
verses.meaning: The same sound, different responses. Some people interpret God's voice as nothing more than natural events. Spiritual hearing requires an open heart.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, give me ears to hear Your voice.
verses.discussion_question: Why did some people hear God's voice and think it was only thunder?
verses.family_discussion: The same voice, two different reactions. What helps a person hear God's voice as God's voice — and not just noise? How is your family cultivating that kind of heart?
verses.do_it_today: Spend 2 minutes in quiet today — not talking, just listening. What does God bring to your heart?
verses.illustration_prompt: A crowd of people reacting to a loud sound from above, some ducking and looking at the sky startled, others pointing up with wonder, a golden light visible high above the crowd, different expressions of awe and confusion. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Jesus answered and said, This voice came not because of me, but for your sakes.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'That voice from heaven was not for Me. It was for you.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'God's voice came for your sake, not Mine.'
verses.meaning: God spoke from heaven for the crowd's benefit — to help them believe. God always reaches toward those who need to hear. His voice is a gift of grace.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for speaking to me.
verses.discussion_question: Why did God speak aloud from heaven for the crowd?
verses.family_discussion: God spoke out loud so people could hear and believe. How does God speak to your family today — through His Word, through prayer, through life?
verses.do_it_today: Open the Bible and read one verse — listening for what God is saying to you today.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus gesturing toward the crowd, pointing upward toward heaven, a gentle reassuring expression, the people around Him looking from Jesus to the sky with new understanding, warm light. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Now is the judgment of this world: now shall the prince of this world be cast out.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'The judgment of this world has come. The ruler of this world — the devil — will be thrown out!'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'The devil's power will be broken. Now is his judgment!'
verses.meaning: The cross was not Jesus' defeat — it was the devil's. What looked like evil winning was actually evil being defeated. The cross is God's ultimate victory.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for winning the victory.
verses.discussion_question: How did Jesus defeat the devil on the cross?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus said the devil would be 'cast out' at the cross. How does knowing Jesus has already won change the way your family faces temptation and fear?
verses.do_it_today: When you face something scary or tempting today, say out loud: 'Jesus has already won!'
verses.illustration_prompt: A scene of spiritual triumph — Jesus standing strong with a shining presence, shadows visibly retreating before Him, a sense of a great battle turning, the darkness being pushed back by radiant light. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'When I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw all people to Myself.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'When I am lifted up, I will draw all people to Me.'
verses.meaning: Jesus was speaking of being lifted up on the cross. But the cross, far from ending His mission, would be the means by which all people — everywhere — are drawn to Him.
verses.memory_phrase: Jesus draws all people to Himself.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, draw me closer to You always.
verses.discussion_question: How does Jesus being lifted up on the cross draw people to Him?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus' greatest act of love — dying on the cross — is what draws people to Him. How does the cross draw your own heart closer to Jesus?
verses.do_it_today: Draw a cross on a piece of paper and write beside it: 'Jesus draws me to Himself.'
verses.illustration_prompt: The silhouette of a cross raised against a radiant golden sky, streams of light flowing outward from it toward people from different nations approaching from all directions, a powerful and glorious scene. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: This he said, signifying what death he should die.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said this to show what kind of death He would die — He would be crucified.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus was telling them He would die on a cross.
verses.meaning: John explains that 'lifted up' referred to crucifixion. Jesus was clear-eyed about His death. He did not stumble into it — He walked toward it with full knowledge.
verses.memory_phrase: Jesus knew and chose the cross.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, You chose the cross for me. Thank You.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important that Jesus chose to die — not just that He died?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus knew exactly what would happen and still went forward. What does it mean to your family that Jesus chose the cross for you personally?
verses.do_it_today: Write the words 'He chose this for me' somewhere you will see them today.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus looking calmly and knowingly toward the distance, the shadow of a cross visible on the ground before Him, His expression resolved and full of love rather than fear. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: The people answered him, We have heard out of the law that Christ abideth for ever: and how sayest thou, The Son of man must be lifted up? who is this Son of man?
verses.little_bible: The crowd said: 'The law says the Messiah lives forever. So why do You say He must be lifted up and die? Who are You really?'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The crowd asked: 'The Messiah lives forever. Why do You say He must die? Who are You?'
verses.meaning: The crowd was confused — they knew Scripture but missed its depth. They expected a Messiah who would reign without suffering. They didn't understand that He would reign through suffering.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me understand who You truly are.
verses.discussion_question: Why did the crowd not understand how Jesus could be both dying and eternal?
verses.family_discussion: The crowd knew Scripture but still missed who Jesus was. How can your family make sure you don't just know Bible facts but truly know Jesus Himself?
verses.do_it_today: Ask God to reveal one new thing about who Jesus really is to you today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A confused crowd of people looking at Jesus with questions on their faces, some with scrolls in hand, pointing at Him and speaking among themselves, Jesus listening calmly. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Then Jesus said unto them, Yet a little while is the light with you. Walk while ye have the light, lest darkness come upon you: for he that walketh in darkness knoweth not whither he goeth.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'I am the Light, and I am with you only a little while longer. Walk in the Light now, before the darkness comes. Those who walk in darkness do not know where they are going.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'Walk in the Light while you can. Darkness makes you lost.'
verses.meaning: Jesus gave a loving warning: respond now, while you still can. Darkness is not just sad — it is dangerous. You lose your way. Light is a gift — don't ignore it.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me walk in Your light today.
verses.discussion_question: What happens when you try to walk somewhere in complete darkness?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus said walking in darkness means you don't know where you are going. How does staying close to Jesus — the Light — keep your family on the right path?
verses.do_it_today: Choose one decision to make today by asking: 'What would Jesus — the Light — say about this?'
verses.illustration_prompt: Two contrasting paths — one bathed in warm golden light with a clear road ahead, one shrouded in darkness where the path cannot be seen, a figure standing at the fork choosing the lighted path. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light. These things spake Jesus, and departed, and did hide himself from them.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'Trust in the Light while you have it, and you will become children of light.' After this, Jesus left and hid Himself from them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'Believe in the Light and become a child of light.' Then He hid Himself.
verses.meaning: Jesus' final public invitation before the cross: become a child of light. Trust Him now. Then He withdrew — the door of public ministry was closing. Urgency matters.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I believe in You — the Light.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to be a child of light?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus gave His final public invitation to believe. As a family, have each person answer: 'Am I a child of light?' What does that look like in how you live?
verses.do_it_today: Live as a child of light today — choose kindness, truth, and love in every situation.
verses.illustration_prompt: Children bathed in warm golden light, expressions joyful and peaceful, walking together in the light with Jesus' presence visible ahead, darkness receding behind them. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: But though he had done so many miracles before them, yet they believed not on him:
verses.little_bible: Even though Jesus had done so many miracles in front of them, many people still refused to believe in Him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus did many miracles. But many people still did not believe.
verses.meaning: Miracles alone do not produce faith. The heart must be willing. Seeing is not the same as believing. Faith is a choice.
verses.memory_phrase: Faith is a choice, not just sight.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I choose to believe in You.
verses.discussion_question: Why might someone see a miracle and still not believe?
verses.family_discussion: People saw miracle after miracle and still refused to trust Jesus. What does it take for a heart to truly believe — beyond seeing signs?
verses.do_it_today: Choose to believe something God has said in His Word even when you cannot see it yet.
verses.illustration_prompt: A crowd of people standing with arms crossed and faces turned away, behind them a scene of miraculous healings and wonders, yet their eyes are averted, stubbornness visible in their posture. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: That the saying of Esaias the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spake, Lord, who hath believed our report? and to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?
verses.little_bible: This happened to fulfil Isaiah the prophet's words: 'Lord, who has believed what we told them? Who has seen God's mighty power?'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: This came true just as Isaiah the prophet said long ago.
verses.meaning: God knew this would happen — Isaiah prophesied it hundreds of years before. The rejection of Jesus was not a surprise to God. Scripture is always fulfilled.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, Your Word always comes to pass.
verses.discussion_question: How does knowing God predicted rejection help you trust He is in control?
verses.family_discussion: Isaiah predicted people would reject God's message — and he was right. How does fulfilled prophecy build your trust that everything God has said will come true?
verses.do_it_today: Read one Old Testament prophecy about Jesus. See how perfectly it was fulfilled.
verses.illustration_prompt: An ancient scroll unrolling beside a scene of Jesus being rejected by a crowd, the words of the scroll glowing, showing the prophecy and the fulfilment side by side. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Therefore they could not believe, because that Esaias said again,
verses.little_bible: They were not able to believe — because Isaiah had also said something else about this.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They could not believe — just as Isaiah had said.
verses.meaning: This verse is a transition. God had spoken through Isaiah about a deeper spiritual hardness. The inability to believe was itself a fulfilment of what God foreknew.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, Your Word is always right and true.
verses.discussion_question: Why can we trust everything God has said in His Word?
verses.family_discussion: God knew long in advance what would happen. How does knowing God sees the future give your family confidence when the world feels confusing?
verses.do_it_today: Tell God: 'I trust that Your Word is true — even when I don't understand everything.'
verses.illustration_prompt: An open ancient scroll glowing with golden letters, a quill beside it, the words pointing toward a fulfillment scene, timeless quality to the image showing old words meeting new events. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.
verses.little_bible: Isaiah said: 'God has let their eyes become blind and their hearts become hard. They cannot see, they cannot understand, they cannot turn and be healed.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Isaiah said: 'Their hearts were hardened so they could not see or understand.'
verses.meaning: This is one of the Bible's most sobering truths: persistent rejection of God hardens the heart. God does not force belief — He honours a hardened heart's choice. Keep your heart soft toward God.
verses.memory_phrase: Keep your heart soft to God.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, keep my heart soft and open to You.
verses.discussion_question: How does a heart get hard toward God?
verses.family_discussion: A heart gets hard when it keeps saying no to God. How can your family protect your hearts from growing hard — staying soft and open to Jesus?
verses.do_it_today: Ask God to show you any part of your heart that might be growing hard. Say yes to Him in that area today.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two contrasting hearts — one stone-grey and cracked, surrounded by darkness, and one warm, glowing softly, held gently in two open hands — representing hardened versus open hearts. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: These things said Esaias, when he saw his glory, and spake of him.
verses.little_bible: Isaiah wrote these words after he had a vision of God's glory. He was speaking about Jesus.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Isaiah saw God's glory in a vision — and he was speaking about Jesus.
verses.meaning: Isaiah saw the glory of the Lord in his famous vision (Isaiah 6). John tells us that what Isaiah saw was the glory of Jesus — the pre-existent, eternal Son of God.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I worship Your eternal glory.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean that Isaiah saw Jesus' glory long before Jesus was born?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus existed long before Bethlehem — Isaiah saw His glory. How does knowing Jesus is eternal change the way your family thinks about Him?
verses.do_it_today: Read Isaiah 6:1-5 together as a family and worship Jesus as the Eternal King.
verses.illustration_prompt: A prophetic vision scene — a man (Isaiah) shielding his eyes before a radiant throne filled with light and glory, angels present, the whole scene pointing forward to the Lord of all. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Nevertheless among the chief rulers also many believed on him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess him, lest they should be put out of the synagogue:
verses.little_bible: Even among the religious leaders, many believed in Jesus secretly. But they would not say so — they were afraid the Pharisees would throw them out of the synagogue.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Some leaders believed in Jesus but were too afraid to say so.
verses.meaning: Secret belief that cannot be confessed is fragile faith. Fear of people silenced what their hearts knew. Believing is not enough if you will not stand for what you believe.
verses.memory_phrase: Do not be a secret believer.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, give me courage to stand for You.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it dangerous to believe in Jesus but keep it secret?
verses.family_discussion: These leaders believed but stayed silent because they feared being rejected. Has your family ever stayed quiet about Jesus to avoid rejection? What is the cost of that silence?
verses.do_it_today: Tell one person today that you believe in Jesus — out loud, not in secret.
verses.illustration_prompt: Several men in official robes standing in a crowd, their faces carrying a hidden belief, glancing at each other uncertainly, while others around them boldly reject Jesus. The internal conflict visible on their faces. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: For they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God.
verses.little_bible: They cared more about what people thought of them than what God thought of them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: They wanted people's praise more than God's praise.
verses.meaning: This is one of the most searching verses in the Gospel: whose praise matters more to you — people's or God's? It is impossible to truly follow Jesus while living for human approval.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, let Your praise matter most to me.
verses.discussion_question: Whose opinion matters most to you — people's or God's?
verses.family_discussion: These leaders chose the praise of people over the praise of God. How does your family make decisions — based on what others will think, or what God thinks?
verses.do_it_today: Before one decision today, ask: 'What does God think about this?' — not 'What will people think?'
verses.illustration_prompt: A person standing between two symbolic figures — one representing the crowd's approval with applause, one representing God's glory shining above — and choosing where to look. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: Jesus cried and said, He that believeth on me, believeth not on me, but on him that sent me.
verses.little_bible: Jesus called out loudly: 'Whoever believes in Me is not just believing in Me alone — they are believing in the Father who sent Me!'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'Believe in Me — and you believe in the Father who sent Me!'
verses.meaning: Jesus and the Father are one. To trust Jesus is to trust God. Faith in the Son is faith in the Father. Jesus does not point to Himself alone — He reveals the Father.
verses.memory_phrase: Believe in Jesus. Believe in God.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, I believe in You and in Your Father.
verses.discussion_question: Why is believing in Jesus the same as believing in God the Father?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus and the Father are one — to know Jesus is to know God. How has knowing Jesus helped your family know what God is like?
verses.do_it_today: Name one thing you know about God the Father because of what Jesus showed you.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus speaking with arms outstretched in declaration, radiant light connecting Him to a heavenly figure above, the crowd listening and some looking upward in wonder. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: And he that seeth me seeth him that sent me.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'When you see Me, you are seeing the Father who sent Me.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'Seeing Me is seeing the Father.'
verses.meaning: Jesus is the perfect image of the invisible God. To look at Jesus — His love, His truth, His holiness — is to see what God is truly like. Jesus is the face of God.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, show me God the Father through You.
verses.discussion_question: What do you learn about God by looking at Jesus?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus shows us exactly what God is like. What is one thing Jesus showed about God's character that means a lot to your family?
verses.do_it_today: Read one story about Jesus today and ask: 'What does this show me about God?'
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus and a glowing figure representing the Father side by side, their faces alike, the Father's glory reflected in Jesus' face, a warm and unified scene of divine love. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: I am come a light into the world, that whosoever believeth on me should not abide in darkness.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'I have come as a Light into the world. Everyone who trusts in Me will not live in darkness.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'I am the Light. Believe in Me and you won't be in the dark.'
verses.meaning: Jesus is the Light that breaks every darkness — sin, fear, confusion, death. Trusting Him means leaving the dark behind. No darkness can remain where the Light of Jesus shines.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are my Light. I believe in You.
verses.discussion_question: What darkness does Jesus drive away when you trust in Him?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus says trusting Him means you won't live in darkness. What areas of your family's life need more of Jesus' light today?
verses.do_it_today: Turn on a light in a dark room — and tell Jesus: 'You are my Light. I trust You.'
verses.illustration_prompt: A child stepping out of a shadow into radiant sunlight, arms open wide, a joyful expression, the light warm and golden and welcoming, the darkness clearly behind them and fading. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: And if any man hear my words, and believe not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'If anyone hears My words and does not believe, I do not judge them now. I did not come to judge the world — I came to save the world.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'I came to save the world, not to judge it — not yet.'
verses.meaning: Jesus came first as Saviour. Judgment will come, but His mission right now is rescue. There is still time to believe. His hand is extended, not raised in judgment.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for coming to save, not to judge.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it good news that Jesus came to save the world?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus came to save — and the door is still open. How can your family take seriously the urgency of sharing the Good News while the time of salvation is still here?
verses.do_it_today: Pray for someone who has not yet trusted Jesus: 'Lord, save them before it is too late.'
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus with hands open and extended toward a person who looks uncertain, warmth and welcome on His face, an open door of light behind Him, no condemnation only invitation. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my words, hath one that judgeth him: the word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'Whoever rejects Me and refuses My words will face judgment. The very words I have spoken will judge them on the last day.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'Rejecting Me has consequences. My words will judge everyone on the last day.'
verses.meaning: Scripture is not just good advice — it is God's authoritative Word. To reject Jesus is not without consequence. His words stand forever and will be the measure on the last day.
verses.memory_phrase: God's Word is the final judge.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me receive Your words and obey them.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it serious to reject Jesus and His words?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus says His words will judge us on the last day. How does your family treat God's Word — as the final authority, or just one opinion among many?
verses.do_it_today: Choose to obey one specific thing Jesus has said in the Bible today.
verses.illustration_prompt: An open glowing Book above a courtroom-like scene, rays of light shining down from its pages as a reminder of the final judgment, solemn and serious atmosphere, the weight of truth made visible. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: For I have not spoken of myself; but the Father which sent me, he gave me a commandment, what I should say, and what I should speak.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'I have not spoken from Myself. The Father who sent Me told Me exactly what to say.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'Every word I speak comes from the Father who sent Me.'
verses.meaning: Jesus' words are not merely human wisdom — they are the very words of God the Father, delivered through the Son. When we read Jesus' words, we are reading what God Himself has said.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, help me hear Your words as God's own words.
verses.discussion_question: How do we know Jesus' words come from God the Father?
verses.family_discussion: Everything Jesus said, He received from the Father. How should this change the way your family reads and listens to what Jesus says in the Gospels?
verses.do_it_today: Read one teaching of Jesus today and sit with it, knowing: these are God's very own words.
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus speaking to a crowd, a gentle beam of light connecting Him to the sky above, representing the Father's voice flowing through Jesus to the people, a sacred and unified scene. Storybook watercolour.

verses.kjv: And I know that his commandment is life everlasting: whatsoever I speak therefore, even as the Father said unto me, so I speak.
verses.little_bible: Jesus said: 'I know that the Father's command is eternal life. So everything I say, I say exactly as the Father told Me to say it.'
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Jesus said: 'God's command is life forever. I speak exactly what the Father tells Me.'
verses.meaning: The chapter ends where it began — with life. God's word is not a burden; it is the path to life everlasting. Jesus perfectly passed on that word, down to the last syllable.
verses.prayer: Lord Jesus, Your words are the words of eternal life.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean that God's commandment is eternal life?
verses.family_discussion: Jesus says obeying God's Word leads to eternal life. How can your family treat God's Word not as a list of rules but as the gift of life itself?
verses.do_it_today: Read one of God's commands from Scripture and say: 'This is the path to life — I will walk it.'
verses.illustration_prompt: Jesus concluding His teaching, light radiating from His presence, the crowd before Him still and attentive, an atmosphere of holy authority and the weight of eternal truth, a golden horizon visible behind Him. Storybook watercolour.
